name: Dexlansoprazole
summary: The R-enantiomer of lansoprazole, delivered in a dual delayed-release capsule that gives two absorption peaks and a longer suppression window.
good: Patients with irregular meal schedules, or breakthrough symptoms later in the day/evening on a standard PPI.
bad: Cost is usually higher than generic single-release PPIs for a benefit that matters mainly when meal timing is genuinely inconsistent.
clinicalPearls: The dual-release profile — not enantiomer purity — is what actually extends coverage; think of it as lansoprazole with built-in second dosing.
mechanism: Same H⁺/K⁺-ATPase target; the innovation is delivery, not the molecule’s target.
pharmacodynamics: Extended duration of pH >4 control compared with single-release PPIs, from the second, delayed drug-release pulse several hours after the first.

pharmacokinetics.onset: First pulse behaves like a standard PPI; the second pulse extends coverage into the afternoon/evening.
pharmacokinetics.duration: Longer effective window than most PPIs from one daily dose, which helps with nocturnal and late-day symptoms.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: CYP2C19/3A4, similar variability considerations to lansoprazole.

indications: GERD, erosive esophagitis healing and maintenance.
interactionNotes: Same general PPI absorption-related and CYP2C19 cautions.
